response.summary: Overall notebook quality is weak despite running end-to-end: the code executes and prints metrics consistently, but there are critical issues in how the model is built and how results are reported. The most important finding is data leakage: the feature scaling is fit on the full dataset before the train/test split, which can artificially inflate performance and makes the evaluation unreliable. There is also a serious mismatch between the written conclusions (claiming 0.97 AUC and 0.91 precision on “fiber customers”) and the actual outputs shown (test AUC around 0.729, with no precision or subgroup analysis computed). In the interview, ask the candidate to explain why preprocessing must be fit only on the training set (e.g., via a pipeline), and to reconcile their stated metrics with what the notebook actually calculates, including how they would compute and validate any subgroup performance claims.
